title: Existence of a versal ring at a finite-residue-field stack point
statement: Let $(R,\mathfrak m_R)$ be a commutative Noetherian local ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], where local means having a unique maximal ideal. Let $k$ be a finite extension of $R/\mathfrak m_R$ [def-weil-field]. Schemes and algebraic spaces are [def-pc-scheme, def-trf-algebraic-space], in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. An algebraic stack is a category fibred in groupoids with effective etale descent for objects and sheaf descent for isomorphisms, diagonal representable by algebraic spaces, and a smooth surjective scheme atlas. Representable means that every scheme-valued 2-base change is an algebraic space. Smoothness is tested on smooth scheme atlases by [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. Locally of finite type means that a smooth scheme atlas has locally finite type composite to the base [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Let $\mathcal X\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ be an algebraic stack locally of finite type and let $x:\operatorname{Spec}k\to\mathcal X$ be an $R$-point [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. For an Artinian local $R$-algebra $A$ with specified residue field $k$, let $\mathcal F_x(A)$ be the groupoid of pairs $(\eta,\alpha)$ with $\eta\in\mathcal X(A)$ and $\alpha:\eta|_k\cong x$, with arrows respecting the marking. Artinian means descending chains of ideals stabilize; all maps between test algebras are local and induce the identity on their specified residue fields. Here a versal ring at $x$ means a complete Noetherian local $R$-algebra $C$ with residue field $k$, equipped with a marked formal object: objects $\eta_n\in\mathcal F_x(C/\mathfrak m_C^n)$, $n\geq1$, with coherent transition isomorphisms $\eta_{n+1}|_{C/\mathfrak m_C^n}\cong\eta_n$. For a test algebra $A$ and a local $R$-map $v:C\to A$ inducing the identity on $k$ (it kills some $\mathfrak m_C^n$), write $\eta_v\in\mathcal F_x(A)$ for the pullback of $\eta_n$ along the induced map $C/\mathfrak m_C^n\to A$. Versality means: for every surjection $A'\twoheadrightarrow A$ of test algebras, every such $v:C\to A$, every $\zeta'\in\mathcal F_x(A')$ and every isomorphism $\zeta'|_A\cong\eta_v$ in $\mathcal F_x(A)$, there exist a local $R$-map $v':C\to A'$ lifting $v$ and an isomorphism $\zeta'\cong\eta_{v'}$ in $\mathcal F_x(A')$ restricting to the prescribed one. Then a versal ring at $x$, with its marked formal object, exists.

proof.text: Choose a finite basis $b_1,\ldots,b_d$ of $k$ over $R/\mathfrak m_R$. Its $R$-linear span is all of $k$, since the coefficients in $R/\mathfrak m_R$ lift to $R$; consequently these elements also generate $k$ as an $R$-algebra. Thus the finite-type-field hypothesis holds. By the Artinian finite-type residue criterion, every test algebra with residue field $k$ is of finite type over $R$.

source.place: Tag 0DQX, lemma-versal-ring, finite type field hypothesis; artin.tex, discussion after definition-RS

proof.text: Apply algebraic-stack Rim–Schlessinger gluing to $\mathcal X$ over $\operatorname{Spec}R$. It gives precisely the equivalence on the Artinian finite-type pushouts required by the general versal-formal-object theorem. The stack hypothesis is in the statement and $R$ is Noetherian; this input requires no extra finite type or separation condition on the stack.

source.place: Tag 0DQX, lemma-versal-ring, existence via lemma-deformation-category; artin.tex Tag 07WQ, lemma-algebraic-stack-RS

proof.text: The given locally finite type smooth atlas and the finite-type $R$-field $k$ satisfy the tangent-finiteness lemma. It identifies the tangent space as the isomorphism classes of pairs $(\eta,\alpha:\eta|_k\cong x)$ over $k[\epsilon]/(\epsilon^2)$ and says it is finite-dimensional. Apply the existing general versal-formal-object theorem to the fibred groupoid $\mathcal X$, using this finiteness and the Rim–Schlessinger property from step 2. It produces a complete Noetherian local $R$-algebra $C$ with residue field $k$, compatible $\xi_n\in\mathcal X(C/\mathfrak m_C^n)$, and a specified $\xi_1\cong x$, with lifting of every prescribed isomorphism across every test-algebra surjection.

source.place: Tag 0DQX, lemma-versal-ring, existence; artin.tex Tag 07X1, lemma-finite-dimension; formal-defos.tex Tag 06IW, lemma-versal-object-existence

proof.text: Give $\xi_n$ the marking obtained by composing its restriction isomorphism $\xi_n|_k\cong\xi_1$ with the specified $\xi_1\cong x$, and call the resulting marked object $\eta_n$. Coherence of the transition isomorphisms makes them arrows respecting these markings. The lifting theorem's isomorphisms respect the special-fibre identifications and extend the prescribed one, so they are exactly the required arrows in $\mathcal F_x(A')$. Its lift $C\to A'$ is local and induces the identity on $k$. Hence this system has every clause of the stated versality condition.
